chapter: Parade bands, instruments and the Eureka band
title: WPA band and the Chum Club with T-Boy
summary: Gabriel names the musicians in his WPA-era band and at Babe Carous's Chum Club.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: That's just to read. Oh, I read them. I mean a box with the reader. I'll get it out there. Anyhow, we played a record band. I played all around with T-Boy and me. We even played. We played the Chum Club. I can't exactly tell you. When I was in the WPA band I can't tell you what year that was because I don't know if it was 1930 or 1933 or 34. I don't know what it was. But anyhow, when I was at WPA I was playing Big Carous Chum Club. T-Boy was playing trumpet. We had Sam Lee playing tenor. Sam Lee, we didn't have a time on it. We had a boy they called Benny Tony from over the river.
He was playing piano. Yeah, he was playing piano.

I was playing the clarinet in the alto. Sam played the tenor in the clarinet. We had Sidney Fusier playing the ghetto or banjo. He could change either one. We would play there every night. We would come on there at 1030. Babe Carous Chum Club, Decayden Toulouse. That was our bunch. We had Roy playing drummer. The boy they called Roy. He stood uptown somewhere named Roy Evans. I think he was. Oh, I've heard of him. He died. Well, that was our drummer. Then we had the barrica band. We would play all them funerals, parade in the band. They had John Cashman. He was a clarinet player. I could play sax with him. See? And he played the clarinet. Couldn't touch the clarinet. He didn't want that. So we played the clarinet. We had Ray playing bass. But it's red, big red. You know Ray? Yeah. And Ray playing with, we had Tillman playing trumpet with us sometime. And Ray Park was that?
